deep.reconstruction:
This page is not part of the EGA VII plan. It is a typescript page (numbered 30, with Grothendieck's handwritten corrections) of the SGA 4 material on points of the étale topos (Exposé VIII, §7), filed among the EGA plan sheets. The numbering 7.9.1 and the content match SGA 4 VIII 7.9, which says that points of X_et correspond to strictly local X-schemes (strict henselizations at geometric points).

Setup. X is a scheme and ξ, ξ' are geometric points. The fibre functor ε_ξ on X_et is the filtered colimit of the functors X_i^∨ : F ↦ F(X_i). Here (X_i) runs over the affine étale neighbourhoods of ξ, so ε_ξ is a pro-object.

Part a) (end): the functor 'geometric point ↦ point of the topos' is fully faithful.
- Formula (*). By Yoneda, Hom(X_i^∨, ε_ξ') = ε_ξ'(X_i) = colim_j Hom_X(X'_j, X_i). Taking the limit over i gives Hom(ε_ξ, ε_ξ') ≅ lim_i colim_j Hom_X(X'_j, X_i).
- Formula (**). The strict henselization X̄(ξ) = Spec O^sh_{X,ξ} is the projective limit lim_i X_i in preschemes; the limit exists because the transition maps are affine. So Hom_X(X̄(ξ'), X̄(ξ)) = lim_i Hom_X(X̄(ξ'), X_i).
- Each X_i is locally of finite presentation over X. By EGA IV 8.14.2, Hom_X(lim_j X'_j, X_i) = colim_j Hom_X(X'_j, X_i). This gives (**) with the same right-hand side as (*).
- Comparing (*) and (**) gives Hom(ε_ξ, ε_ξ') ≅ Hom_X(X̄(ξ'), X̄(ξ)), up to compatibility checks left to the reader.

Part b): essential surjectivity. Every point of X_et should come from a geometric point. Lemma 7.9.1 starts this: if C is a site with finite projective limits and E = C~ its topos, then every fibre functor φ on E is a cofiltering limit of the pro-system of functors Y^∨ (F ↦ F(Y) = Hom(Ỹ, F)), indexed by the category C_φ of pairs (Y, ξ) with ξ ∈ φ(Ỹ). C_φ is cofiltering because φ commutes with finite limits; this is the 'pseudo-filtrante connexe' condition. This is the standard 'category of elements / pro-representability of points' argument of SGA 4 IV 6.8.

The page breaks off at the definition of C_φ. A margin note by part b) seems to read 'pas d'urgence'.
errors: In the line before (**) the typescript reads Hom_X(X_j, X_i); it should be Hom_X(X'_j, X_i), as in (*) and (**).
Unstated hypotheses: the X_i must be taken affine (or with affine transition maps) so that lim X_i exists and EGA IV 8.14.2 applies; the compatibility of the two bijections is left unchecked.

ideas.what: Morphisms between the fibre functors of geometric points correspond to X-morphisms between strict henselizations (contravariantly).
ideas.modern_name: Points of the étale topos = strictly local schemes / specialization of geometric points

ideas.what: Hom out of a projective limit of schemes into a scheme locally of finite presentation is the colimit of the Homs.
Any point of a topos C~, for C with finite limits, is pro-represented by the cofiltering category of elements C_φ.
ideas.modern_name: Points of a topos as flat (filtering) functors / pro-objects
ideas.where_published: SGA 4, Exposé IV §6 (6.8), used in Exposé VIII 7.9

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft typescript page of SGA 4 VIII §7.9 (points of the étale topos), apparently misfiled with the EGA VII plan. The content is entirely published and standard; the only points of interest are archival (misfiling, the 'pas d'urgence' margin note).
transcription_corrections: The image indeed shows 'Hom_X(X_j, X_i)' without a prime in the line before (**); this is a typo in the original, not a transcription error.
The definitions are typed with '==' (X̄(ξ) == lim X_i, Y^∨(F) == F(Y)), Grothendieck's notation for 'equal by definition'.
The margin note next to b) is circled and probably reads 'pas d'urgence'.
There is a page number '3' at the bottom left; the left margin repeats the corrected symbols (φ, ε_ξ', ', t', 'e e', ']['), which are typist instructions, not mathematics.
